what: Ryder leases and maintains trucks for companies that would rather not own a fleet, runs warehouses and distribution for them, and moves freight as a broker.
customers: Manufacturers, retailers and distributors who need trucks and warehouses but not the staff to run them.
money: warehousing and dedicated transport for customers
drivers and trucks assigned to one customer
moat: A maintenance network of hundreds of shops that an individual fleet owner cannot replicate, plus the scale to buy and resell trucks better than its customers can.
risks: Used truck resale values set a large part of the profit, and they have been falling
$8.7B of debt, inherent in a leasing business but large against a $10.8B market value
Freight volumes have been weak for two years
opportunities: 11.3 times free cash flow with $954M of free cash flow
Lease contracts run for years, so most revenue does not move with the freight cycle
Revenue grew from $9.7B to $12.7B in four years and the dividend has been paid for decades
watch: Used vehicle sales results and contractual lease revenue growth.
